title: Thanthai Periyar and the Chengalpattu Conference: Women's Rights and Equal Inheritance (1929)
summary: In February 1929, at the historic First Provincial Self-Respect Conference in Chengalpattu, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy pioneered radical resolutions demanding equal property rights for women.
full_text:
On February 17 and 18, 1929, in the town of Chengalpattu near Madras, Periyar E. V. Ramasamy convened the First Provincial Self-Respect Conference, marking a watershed moment in the history of Asian feminism.

In an era when women were confined to domestic servitude, denied higher education, and deprived of property rights under customary law, Periyar tabled an astonishing series of radical resolutions:
1. Daughters must possess absolute equality with sons in ancestral property inheritance.
2. Women must have equal access to all public employment, including the police and military.
3. Marriages must be stripped of priestcraft and expensive dowry rituals, based solely on mutual consent.
4. Women must have equal rights to initiate legal divorce from abusive marriages.

Orthodox critics were scandalized, warning that granting financial autonomy to women would destroy the sacred institution of the Hindu family.

Periyar responded with devastating clarity:
"If a social institution can survive only by chaining half of humanity to domestic slavery, then that institution does not deserve to exist! Can a cart travel forward when one wheel is free and the other is deliberately shattered?
Until women enjoy economic independence and equal property rights, talks of national freedom and human dignity are mere hypocrisy! Self-respect is not a male monopoly; it is the birthright of womanhood."

The visionary resolutions drafted by Periyar in 1929 anticipated international conventions by decades, ultimately becoming statutory law when Tamil Nadu passed the landmark Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act of 1989.
